report.summary: Reviewed scheduler.py chunk 2 of 2: gate() returns [] when no writes; spawn()/configure() docstrings kept; main() JSON keys uncheckable; no defects found.
risks: scheduler.py:0 | medium | gate() docstring says it returns a list of gated TaskAttempts, but the code returns [] when no writes; callers may not expect an empty list as a success signal. | Inspect callers in dispatch() to confirm empty list is handled.
scheduler.py:0 | low | main() JSON output keys are not pinned by any schema; consumers may break if keys change. | Check for a documented JSON contract or tests that assert on the JSON keys.

scheduler.py:0 | low | configure() docstring says 'mint or reshape' but the code returns config via reg.get_role(name, repo_root); if the role is not found after creation, config is None. | Verify create_role always stores the role such that get_role finds it immediately.

handoff.purpose: Review gate(), spawn(), configure(), _demo_tasks(), and main() in the second half of the scheduler module.

symbols.name: gate
symbols.note: Accepts tasks, filters accepted write-mode attempts, returns gate_candidates result or [] if no writes.

symbols.name: spawn
symbols.note: Decomposes objective, then plans (dry_run) or dispatches (live).

symbols.name: configure
symbols.note: Creates or updates an agent role via agents_registry, returns summary dict.

symbols.name: _demo_tasks
symbols.note: Converts benchmark TASKS into objective/paths dicts.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry: builds scheduler, plans demo tasks, prints or JSON-dumps plan.

claims.text: Landing a candidate this returns into repo_root is a SEPARATE, explicit act -- see promote_candidates and the comment on can_parallel in dispatch for why this method does not do that itself.
claims.why: The claim references promote_candidates and dispatch, which are outside this chunk; cannot verify against this code.

claims.text: One-shot entry: decompose a single objective into subtasks, then plan (dry_run) or dispatch (live) them across the bounded local bench.
claims.why: spawn() calls decompose(), then returns plan() if dry_run else dispatch().

claims.text: This is the dynamic counterpart to the hardcoded _demo_tasks flow -- the subtasks come from decompose (local model with a deterministic per-path fallback), not a fixed list.
claims.why: The claim about decompose's fallback behavior is not observable in this chunk; only the call is visible.

claims.text: Dynamic agent configurator: mint or reshape an agent-role definition at runtime.
claims.why: configure() either creates a new role or updates an existing one via reg.create_role/update_role.

claims.text: Ikarus owns the crew roster, so creating/editing roles is his job -- routing (router.load_agents) picks up the change with no restart.
claims.why: The claim about router.load_agents is outside this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: Returns a summary; raises ValueError on an invalid spec.
claims.why: The function returns a summary dict, but whether it raises ValueError on invalid spec depends on reg.create_role/update_role, which are not in this chunk.

observations.what: gate() returns [] when there are no accepted write-mode attempts, despite the docstring implying it returns gated candidates; this is a silent early return.
main() prints plan['waves'] but the JSON output also includes 'waves'; the format is not pinned by any schema visible in this chunk.

configure() returns 'config': reg.get_role(name, repo_root) which may be None if the role is not found immediately after creation; the docstring promises a summary but not a guarantee of non-None config.
